note.question: How do real-time delivery time forecasting and promising interact in online retailing?
note.overview: Providing fast and reliable delivery services is key to running a successful online retail business. To achieve a better delivery time guarantee policy, we study how to estimate and promise delivery time for new customer orders in real time. Delivery time promising is critical to managing customer expectations and improving customer satisfaction.

components.formal: Decision rule: When there are only two classes (e.g., positive and negative), the decision rule simply decides a threshold on the positive probability: predict a positive class when the positive probability is above the threshold.
conditions: The estimated probabilities {ˆp(k | x),k ∈K} form the basis of promised delivery time (in days) management.

For instance, the usual decision rule that tends to maximize the accuracy is to predict the class with the highest posterior probability, that is, the classifier predicts that order x arrives on the kth day if ˆp(k | x) > ˆp(j | x) for j ≠k.
The typical decision rule is to predict class according to a weighted posterior probability: arg maxk{ωk · ˆp(k | x)}, where the weights {ωk,k ∈K} must be learned to minimize the expected cost.
